laws.rule: Puerto Princesa Underground River (Palawan) runs a no permit, no entry policy: every visitor needs a Visitor Entry Permit from the Underground River Booking Office before going to the park, with a cap of 900 visitors a day and tours only from 8 am to 4 pm. The park says staying overnight in Sabang or turning up at the park does not guarantee a permit.
laws.heading: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, Notice to the Public (9 January 2026)

laws.rule: At the Underground River, feeding or teasing the macaques is prohibited, and park signs say no swimming and no smoking. The park advises not bringing food or plastic bags on the tour.

Underground River Visitor Entry Permits are bought at the PPUR booking office (City Coliseum, Barangay San Pedro, Puerto Princesa) before going to the park; the city tourism page lists PHP 175 to PHP 250 (about A$3.90 to about A$5.58, RBA rate of 30 October 2026). No permit, no entry.
laws.heading: PPUR, how to get there

laws.rule: At Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, the Tubbataha Management Office says divemasters may not use cameras or video while diving, so they can focus on their duties. Confirm current conditions with the park and operator; this statement is specifically about divemasters.

local-law.note: Underground River only. The fee range is from the city tourism page, which is undated and may be out of date. El Nido's eco-tourism fee could not be read on the municipal site (bot check) and is not recorded; Coron's fee had no official page.

layers.authority: Municipality of El Nido, Palawan (Sangguniang Bayan Ordinance No. 20, Series of 2024)
layers.process: El Nido charges an Eco-Tourism Development Fee to people who are not residents of the municipality. The municipality's website says an ordinance raised it from PHP 200 to PHP 400, and that the ticket gives access to the municipality's tourism sites for 10 days (a 2009 notice; the period may have changed). Palawan residents from outside El Nido paid a lower rate in that earlier notice. The municipal page could not be reread in full today, so the enactment date (the site gives 8 July 2025 and also a December 2025 post) and the current amount should be confirmed with the El Nido tourism office. This is a municipal rule held here because El Nido has no place record of its own.

Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park: all entrants need a Visitor Entry Permit before entering, with the applicable conservation fee paid before issue. The park lists visitor and vessel permits separately. Confirm with the Tubbataha Management Office and the trip operator who submits each permit.

Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park: the park lists a PHP5,000 conservation fee per visitor (about A$111.51 at the RBA rate of A$1 = PHP44.84 on 30 October 2026). Children aged 12 and under are exempt from the conservation fee. Check current fees and whether they are included in the operator price before paying.

Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park: the boat owner, operator, captain or representative must secure a Vessel Entry Permit before entering. Vessel fees vary by gross tonnage and are separate from visitor conservation fees; travellers should confirm the arrangement with their operator.

Commercial tour operators at Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park must secure a Permit to Operate at least two months before their first scheduled entry. Vessel, safety, business and diver accreditation documents are among the published requirements. Ask the Tubbataha Management Office for the current application process.

The Tubbataha Management Office lists requirements for foreign crew or divemasters employed by commercial boat operators, including a Special Working Permit or Alien Employment Card. Confirm eligibility and current immigration and labour conditions with the relevant authorities before accepting work.
